title: Code Style and Maintainability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Code Style and Maintainability”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Consistent indentation” under lesson 164, “Code Style and Maintainability”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Code Style and Maintainability”?
options: Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review.
questions.answer_key: Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review.
questions.explanation: Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Code Style and Maintainability”?
options: Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
